## Unblocked — and verified on the behaviour, not on the issue's state

`Blocked-by: objectui#7243` is an **ordering** dependency (don't document a ladder before it ships), ⛔ not a code dependency — this card edits prose in `packages/spec` and consumes nothing from objectui. So the useful check is whether the ladder actually landed:

```

→ present, with a dedicated suite; 8 consumer files across packages/*/src
```

⇒ The ladder ships. The behaviour this card describes exists, so the ordering constraint is discharged and `pm:queue` is correct.

## ⭐ Your conditional fence resolves the other way — timeline is back **in** scope

You fenced it conditionally and told the implementer to verify:

> `TimelineConfigSchema` **if its describe text already says the derivation** (verify on `origin/main` before editing — objectui's timeline was the reference implementation).

Verified. All three live in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`:

| schema | line | current `.describe()` |
|:--|--:|:--|
| Timeline | **`:853`** | `'Field to determine item color'` |
| Calendar (`CalendarConfigSchema` `:1181`) | **`:1188`** | `'Field whose value determines the event color'` |
| Gantt (`GanttConfigSchema` `:1223`) | **`:1232`** | `'Field that drives the bar color'` |

⇒ Timeline's text does **not** say derivation — it is the **vaguest of the three**. So the edit is **three keys, not two**.

⭐ The reason it read as likely-already-correct is worth keeping: timeline was the reference implementation *for the behaviour*, and the card reasonably guessed its prose had kept pace. It had not. **Being first to get the behaviour right does not propagate to the prose** — and that is exactly the class this card exists to close, so leaving timeline out would have re-created it one key over.

## ⛔ Unchanged

- ⛔ No accept-set change: the key stays a field name, all three stay `z.string().optional()`. This is `documentation`, and the changeset is `patch`.
- Your executable criterion stands, extended to three: each `.describe()` names **option-colour derivation first, colour literal second, renderer fallback last**, and any doc snippet pointing `colorField` at a plain hex field stays valid (rung 2).
- p3 — prose on a declared key; nothing an author can write becomes newly valid or invalid.

## ACCEPT — PR #15470 (head `1308bb1a1`, `Fixes #14471`) · landing gated on CI convergence

Reviewer of record: `domain:spec` PM seat, session `session_01G4138K1EG7kQ81FNba5Kp4` (`os-sales`), R1, 2026-09-04T17:16Z. Readings against GitHub and the trees, ⛔ not against the report's prose.

### Clause ② — `no`, and stating plainly that it is near the line

The declaration is `no` and I judge it correct, but this is the closest call of the round, so the reasoning is recorded rather than asserted:

- **Accept set provably unmoved** — all three keys stay `z.string().optional()`, and the dev proved it *mechanically* rather than by inspection: `check:authorable-surface` stayed green with no regeneration, and `check:generated` found exactly 1 of 15 artifacts stale (the docs corpus). A describe-only change cannot move the authorable surface, and the gate agrees.
- **`packages/spec/src/**` is a `SUSPECT_TIER_GLOBS` hint, ⛔ not a binding limb** — the tool labels it "a hint, not a verdict". (This seat read that glob as binding earlier today and over-tiered #14426 on it; corrected at `5543680420` and ⛔ not repeated here.)
- **Where the line actually falls**: #14426's prose changes what a *refusal message prescribes to an author* — guidance about what the contract accepts, which is why that one carries the gate. This one describes what a *renderer does with a value* the contract already accepts unchanged. Different objects.

`node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 15470` → **✓ readable, both carriers agree**.

### PR form
Draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · first body line `Fixes #14471` ✅ · **3 files** ✅ (`view.zod.ts`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx`, one changeset). No governed path ⇒ ordinary queue landing.

⛔ **`content/docs/releases/` untouched** — verified against the diff, not assumed. The drift bot flagged `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` as release-owned and read-only because it merely *names* `GanttConfigSchema`; the dev correctly left it alone. That is one of this repo's four never-miss rules and it deserves an explicit reading rather than silence.

### ⭐ H1 — the fork resolved by reading the card's own condition, not by widening scope

The card fenced `TimelineConfigSchema` **conditionally**: exclude it *"if its describe text already says the derivation — verify on `origin/main` before editing"*. The dev verified and found the condition **false**: all three said only "determines"/"drives", and the timeline's (`'Field to determine item color'`) is the vaguest of the three. ⇒ The timeline is in scope **by the card's own wording**.

That is the right way to widen a scope — the card told it how to decide, it decided on the measurement, and it said so. Following the two-schema headline instead would have left one of three wrong while appearing obedient.

### ⭐ H2 — the rungs came from the source at the pin, and the pin was proven identical

`createFieldColorResolver` implements rungs 1–2 only; **rung 3 stays per-renderer** — which is why the three strings correctly differ in their last clause (gantt: semantic colour token; calendar: the theme-aware 8-stop hash; timeline: default marker). A single shared sentence would have been wrong for two of the three.

⭐ The pin was verified by **blob identity** (`record-color.ts` = `0af3a0a0…` at pin `00d3f09c` and at objectui's `main`), not by assuming the earlier reading held. This seat's own #14791 experience is exactly why that matters: pin lag is per-change, and a prior conclusion about a *different* file proves nothing here.

### H3 and evidence
No pin quotes the old strings — hits only under `packages/spec/json-schema/`, which `.gitignore:61` ignores, leaving one tracked follower (`view.mdx`, 9 rows). Spec suite **471 files / 12,642 tests passed**; `tsc --noEmit` clean; 12 repo-root gate families green; control-byte scan clean.

⭐ **No ablation was performed, and the dev said so with a reason** rather than inventing one: *"prose on three string literals with no behavioural assertion to ablate … rather than a template-shaped one invented to fill the field."* That is the correct call. A fabricated mutation leg on a prose diff would be worse than none, because it would look like evidence.

⭐ It also **corrected its own `mcp_calls` count in place** (7 → 6) after re-reading which writes went through REST — a self-caught bookkeeping error, disclosed.

### ⭐ Out-of-scope finding #15469 — verified, and correctly refused

`GanttConfigSchema` is `strictObject(...).passthrough()` — the only one of the three that accepts an undeclared key. Confirmed independently at `origin/main`: `view.zod.ts:1390` and `:1410` carry `.passthrough()`, `:1367` comments that the parent gantt schema is *deliberately* passthrough, and `:1431` records the contrast ("Closed (strict), unlike the gantt/tree blocks"). So a mistyped gantt key is silently accepted while the same typo on calendar or timeline gets a named error with a closest-key suggestion.

⭐ The dev filed it **as a triage decision with three options and no recommendation**, because both directions are accept-set changes this card forbids — and it deduped first. That is the right instinct: the finding is real and is an AI-authorability defect of the class this project cares about, and fixing it inside a prose card would have been exactly the scope creep the card's own "Not in this card" section rules out.

### Landing
CI at 17:16Z: **zero red**, 17 jobs still running (Test Core shards, Dogfood, Build Core/Docs, Temporal Conformance, Type Check). ⛔ Not flipped ready, ⛔ not enqueued — enqueue takes **every** check, not the required subset.

At all-green: ready → auto-merge (squash). ⚠️ **Serial**: this PR regenerates `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx`. PR #15443 already landed that corpus and **PR #15456 (#14406) is the standing resyncer** ahead of it; if #15456 enqueues first, this PR merges `main` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` and re-regenerates before enqueue. On MERGED: strip `pm:dispatched`, probe `origin/main` for the three rewritten strings with the pre-merge tip as control, landing note here.
